name: Poratha
overview: Poratha is a male figure identified in Scripture primarily as the son of Haman, as recorded in Esther 9:8. There is no additional information regarding his tribe or other personal details. His mention is brief and specific to his familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Poratha appears only once in Scripture, in Esther 9:8, with no given meaning or divine attribution. Therefore, the name is presented plainly without further significance revealed in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Poratha is explicitly identified as the son of Haman. Scripture does not provide any other family relationships or details beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Poratha's significance lies in his identification as a son of Haman, a key antagonist in the book of Esther. His mention underscores the familial ties of Haman's lineage, which is relevant to the narrative of the Jewish people's deliverance. While Poratha himself does not have a detailed role, his existence contributes to the fuller understanding of Haman's family as presented in the biblical account.
